The design is using a cache instead of each time listing all the PVCs to see VAC usage. This PR is using Lister only?

@sunnylovestiramisu 

It uses informer cache and custom index instead of maintaining another cache. It follows the pvc-protection-controller style.

In the controller manager, only pv controller has to need another cache instead of informer caches. Why does it need those caches, please see [this doc](https://courageous-begonia-1b47e6.netlify.app/docs/components/binder-controller/#local-cache).

Maintaining an another cache is unnecessary for the vac-protection-controller. And informer cache is enough for the vac-protection-controller. It is simpler and easier to implement, while also saving more memory.

> This PR is using Lister only?

the pv/pvc listers should be removed because it's not used. the getPVsAssignedToVAC and getPVCsAssignedToVAC funcs use indexer to list pvc/pv.

> The design is using a cache instead of each time listing all the PVCs to see VAC usage.

Listing objects from informer cache won't call the kube-apiserver.

@carlory we are trying to avoid the pvc protection controller style because of this issue:  https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/109282#issuecomment-2000019682 

Our customers have ran into this a few times and we are looking into changing the existing pvc controller protection logic.

This PR only finds PVs/PVCs objects from informers (local cache), and never asks api server. it shouldn't have a performance issue. but the current implementation has the race condition, as @jsafrane said in https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4529#discussion_r1521198356.

If we want to solve the race, listing objects from kube-apiserver is the only way. It will be a performance issue and worse than pvc protection controller.

There is no good solution for this performance issue. cc @sunnylovestiramisu

@carlory discussed offline with @msau42, we do not want to list from api server for accuracy for now, since we stated in the https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/4529/files that this is a best effort operation.

This is not a one way door either, if after the feature implemented, there are customers asking for accuracy, we can revisit the decision here.

issue_context.body:
### What would you like to be added?
Tasks -- 1. Check finalizers for delete VolumeAttributesClass 2. Creating PVC with VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_admission_controller adding finalizer to VAC for protection 3. Updating PVC with VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_admission_controller adding finalizer to VAC for protection 4. Deleting PVC with VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_protection_controller for deletion 5. Unbound PV created with a VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_admission_controller adding finalizer to VAC for protection 6. Deleting a PV with a VolumeAttributesClass * Vac_protection_controller for deletion
### Why is this needed? Task tracking for kep-3751 https://github.com/kubernetes/enhancements/pull/3780 Task board: https://github.com/orgs/kubernetes-csi/projects/72/views/1
comments: Since the PR for https://github.com/kubernetes/kubernetes/issues/119297 is in a good shape, I will start working on this based on the change.

Hi @msau42, @sunnylovestiramisu, I have a question about this feature. Do we really need the protection for VAC resources? 

Currently, we only protect the PV/PVC resources from being deleted via the `StorageObjectInUseProtection` admission plugin. It makes sure that existing workloads run as expected and do not get affected by the deletion of the PV/PVC resources unless workloads are also deleted.

However, deleting a VAC resource won't affect any existing workloads. PV/PVC can be deleted regardless of whether VAC exists. So why we need to protect VAC resources? 

BTW, the StorageClass resource are not protected as well.

@carlory I was thinking because VAC has certain params, if it is deleted and you only looked at the name of the VAC in PV/PVC, you do not really know what did VAC set.

But for StorageClass, the parameters are mostly preserved?

Based on the issue triage meeting on [Feb 7, 2024](https://docs.google.com/document/d/1n-dXXvCbHsPfO1yrKwT1qoC80KhsxHYKbRdChdzqeXY/edit), we need to have a detailed proposal before implementing it.

> Conclusion: add finalizer now; use informers; document races possible; can we add this in an existing controller, resizer?

The open question is that can we put this in the resizer: when we process modify volume, we can add/remove the finalizer.

Then we also need to add some logic into provisioner to handle add/remove finalizer in the create/delete flow.

/cc @liggitt

Does the controller only start when the feature gate is enabled? Because the beta API is optional, I believe if you start the informer and the API is not installed, then there will be lots of error messages.
Nit: can this func be defined outside the NewVACProtectionController?
If so, the controller has to add a field to hold the indexer.
Hmm okay and it is only used within the controller.
Should we delete the Indexers here for the vacNameKeyIndex?

why to delete the indexer?

If an object is removed from the informer, we will never re-get the item via an indexer.
And the entry of the indexer will be removed automatically? Or it will dangling around in some Get calls?

> And the entry of the indexer will be removed automatically?

Yes. 

> Or it will dangling around in some Get calls?

No.
Nit: should this be "deleting VAC" instead of "deleted VAC"?
will do
Do we need to handle Add? Same question with PV handler?

Assume that a pvc or pv is created with a given vac.

- If the vac doesn't exist, do nothing because we cannot assign a finalizer to the non-existent object.
- If the vac exists, the event handlers of vac informers should handle the finalizer in L81.
- If the vac exists but the informer isn't observed, the finalizer will be added once the event arrives.

So I don't add AddFunc to pvc/pv informers.
Should we check pvcs first or pvs first? Does the order matter here?
The PVC object is deleted before pv object. So, checking the pv object firstly may accelerate to find the answer.
